assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table contains: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = '< 0.11.14 (versions before 0.11.14)', Fixed version = 0.11.14 (lines 49-58).

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 73-74 under '### Ecosystem detection': 'The vulnerable library **quinn-proto** is a Rust crate. Based on the Ecosystem Mappings tables in the security-matrix.md files, the ecosystem is **Cargo**.' Further elaborated on line 76: 'Cargo is classified as a **source dependency ecosystem**'.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md lines 7-8 explicitly state: 'The version impact analysis checks ALL versions from ALL streams in the supportability matrix.' The table lists 7 versions across 2 streams: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). Both affected and unaffected versions are included. The summary on lines 30-32 confirms cross-stream coverage.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md includes a 'Pinned Tag' column with specific tags per version: v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12. Lines 7-9 state: 'Each version's quinn-proto dependency version is extracted from the lock file at the pinned commit tag from the supportability matrix (not branch HEAD).' Line 24 shows the extraction method: 'git show <tag>:Cargo.lock | grep -A2 "name = "quinn-proto""' at the pinned commit tag.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md version 2.2.2 row shows: Pinned Tag = v0.4.9, quinn-proto = '--', Affected = YES, Notes = 'retag of 2.2.1 (same backend tag v0.4.8)'. Lines 25-26 confirm: 'Version 2.2.2 is a retag of 2.2.1 (identical backend tag v0.4.8), so the lock file check is skipped and the result is carried forward from 2.2.1 per Important Rule 5.'

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md lines 33-34 show the diff: 'Current: [RHTPA 2.0.0] / Proposed: [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]'. Lines 36-38 provide rationale: 'PSIRT assigned RHTPA 2.0.0, which does not correspond to any version in the supportability matrix. Lock file analysis at pinned commits confirms:' followed by per-version lock file evidence (lines 40-45). Line 66 reiterates the diff: 'Corrected Affects Versions: [RHTPA 2.0.0] -> [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]'.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md line 20-21: 'Version IDs are discovered at runtime — no hardcoded Jira version IDs are used (Important Rule 6).' The proposed mutation on lines 50-57 uses placeholder IDs '<RHTPA-2.2.0-jira-id>' etc. Lines 59-61 clarify: 'Version IDs above are placeholders — actual IDs would be resolved from the getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields response at runtime using the version names RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, and RHTPA 2.2.2.' The diff and rationale sections consistently use version names (RHTPA 2.2.0, etc.) not numeric IDs.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Task 1: '## Repository' = 'backend' (line 39), '## Target Branch' = 'release/0.4.z' (line 43), '## Acceptance Criteria' with 3 checkboxes (lines 69-73), '## Dependencies' referencing TC-8001 (line 81). Task 2: '## Repository' = 'rhtpa-release.0.4.z' (line 136), '## Target Branch' = 'main' (line 140), '## Acceptance Criteria' with 2 checkboxes (lines 159-161), '## Dependencies' referencing upstream-task-key and TC-8001 (lines 169-170). Blocks linkage on lines 228-234.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md creates exactly two tasks: 'Task 1: Upstream Backport Task' (line 22) and 'Task 2: Downstream Propagation Subtask' (line 117). Lines 228-234 show the Blocks dependency: 'jira.create_link(inwardIssue: <upstream-task-key>, outwardIssue: <downstream-task-key>, type: "Blocks")'. data-extraction.md line 77 confirms the rationale: 'Cargo is classified as a **source dependency ecosystem**, which means remediation produces **two tasks** per stream'.

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: Consistent 'proposed' framing throughout: data-extraction.md line 5: 'the following early assignment actions are proposed'; affects-versions.md line 33: 'Proposed Affects Versions correction'; affects-versions.md line 47: 'Proposed Jira mutation (requires engineer confirmation)'; affects-versions.md line 63: 'Proposed comment'; remediation.md line 24: 'Proposed Jira creation'; remediation.md line 119: 'Proposed Jira creation'; remediation.md line 236: 'Propose transitioning TC-8001 to In Progress'; remediation.md line 238: 'Propose adding the ai-cve-triaged label'. No evidence of executed mutations anywhere.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 3-41 contain '## Step 0.7 — Assign and Transition to Assigned' which appears BEFORE '## Step 1 — CVE Data Extraction' (line 45). Step 0.7 describes: (1) retrieving current user's account ID via jira.user_info() (line 8-10), (2) assigning TC-8001 to the current user via jira.edit_issue (lines 12-15), (3) discovering the Assigned transition dynamically via jira.get_transitions (lines 17-22), (4) transitioning to Assigned status via jira.transition_issue (lines 24-30). Line 34 confirms: 'TC-8001 is currently in **New** status, so the transition to Assigned is applicable.'
